prompt: Based on the Kestrel-9 framing protocol documentation, write a Python function decode_frames(data) that takes a string with one or more concatenated frames and returns a list with the decoded payloads, in order.
reference_doc_content:
Kestrel-9 documentation -- Framing protocol

The Kestrel-9 framing protocol packs one or more messages into a single string, with no separators between frames. Each frame has the format <length>:<payload>, where <length> is the length in characters of the payload that follows, written in decimal (it may have one or more digits), followed by ':' and then exactly that many payload characters. The next frame starts immediately afterwards, with no space or separator. Example: "5:hello3:foo" contains two frames: "hello" (length 5) and "foo" (length 3).
reference_solution:
def decode_frames(data):
    result = []
    i = 0
    n = len(data)
    while i < n:
        colon = data.index(':', i)
        length = int(data[i:colon])
        start = colon + 1
        end = start + length
        result.append(data[start:end])
        i = end
    return result
test_code:
def check(candidate):
    assert candidate("5:hello3:foo") == ["hello", "foo"]
    assert candidate("0:3:abc") == ["", "abc"]
    assert candidate("11:hello world") == ["hello world"]
    assert candidate("") == []
    assert candidate("1:a1:b1:c") == ["a", "b", "c"]
